summary: When someone is found killed and no one knows who did it, judges from the Great Beis Din go out to see which city is closest. Rabbi Yehuda says five judges go out, not three.
stIntro: In certain cases of unsolved murder, the Torah prescribes a ritual performed with

chunks.en: The eglah arufah
chunks.st: a heifer whose neck is broken.
chunks.stMore: During the course of this ritual, the judges say a confession

words.note: Eglah arufah: a special calf brought when someone is found dead and no one knows who killed him.

chunks.en: is said in Hebrew,
chunks.st: in the sacred tongue, Hebrew,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Devarim 21):
chunks.st: as it is stated in the verse:

chunks.en: "If a person who was killed is found in the land...
chunks.st: “If one be found slain in the land
chunks.stMore: which the Lord your God has given you to possess it, lying in the field, and it is not known who has smitten him;

chunks.en: your elders and your judges shall go out."
chunks.st: then your Elders and your judges shall come forth” (Deuteronomy 21:1–2).

chunks.en: Three judges from the Great Beis Din
chunks.st: What is the procedure for this ritual? Three members of the High Court [Sanhedrin]

chunks.en: in Yerushalayim would go out.
chunks.st: that is in Jerusalem would go out to see the corpse.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: five,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: Five would go out,

chunks.en: because it says "your elders" —
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Your Elders,”

chunks.en: that is two; "and your judges" —
chunks.st: in the plural form, indicating at least two; and it is written: “And your judges,”

chunks.en: that is two more. And a Beis Din may not have an even number,
chunks.st: in the plural form, indicating another two judges; and a court may not be comprised of an even
chunks.stMore: number of judges because they need to be able to issue a majority ruling.

chunks.en: so they add one more.
chunks.st: Consequently, they add to them one more Elder.

summary: The eglah arufah is brought only when the person is found lying in a field, and only near a city that has a Beis Din. Yerushalayim never brings one.

chunks.en: If he was found hidden under a pile of stones,
chunks.st: was found concealed in a pile of stones,

chunks.en: or hanging on a tree,
chunks.st: or hanging on a tree,

chunks.en: or floating on the water,
chunks.st: or floating on the surface of the water,

chunks.en: they would not do the eglah arufah,
chunks.st: then the judges would not break the neck of the heifer,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "in the land" —
chunks.st: as it is stated: “If one be found slain in the land” (Deuteronomy 21:1),

chunks.en: and not hidden under a pile;
chunks.st: and not concealed in a pile of stones;

chunks.en: "lying" — and not hanging on a tree;
chunks.st: “lying” on the ground and not hanging on a tree;

chunks.he: בַּשָּׂדֶה, וְלֹא צָף עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם.
chunks.en: "in the field" — and not floating on the water.
chunks.st: “in the field,” and not floating on the surface of the water.

chunks.en: If he was found near the border,
chunks.st: If a corpse was found close to the border of the country,

chunks.en: or near a city where most people are not Jewish,
chunks.st: or close to a city in which the majority of its inhabitants are gentiles,

chunks.he: אוֹ לְעִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ בֵּית דִּין,
chunks.en: or near a city that has no Beis Din,
chunks.st: or close to a city that is without a rabbinical court of twenty-three judges,

chunks.en: they would not do the eglah arufah.
chunks.st: then the judges would not break the heifer’s neck.

chunks.en: They measure only from a city
chunks.st: Additionally, the Elders measure the distance from the corpse only to a city

chunks.en: that has a Beis Din.
chunks.st: that has a rabbinical court with twenty-three judges.

chunks.en: If he was found exactly between two cities,
chunks.st: If the slain person is found precisely between two cities,

chunks.en: both cities bring two calves,
chunks.st: the inhabitants of the two of them bring two heifers total;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Eliezer.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: And Yerushalayim does not bring an eglah arufah.
chunks.st: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not bring a heifer whose neck is broken,
chunks.stMore: even if Jerusalem is the city closest to the slain victim.

summary: If the person was found in two places, Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva argue about which part is brought to the other before they measure.

chunks.en: If one part of him was found in one place
chunks.st: head of the corpse was found in one place

chunks.en: and the rest of him in another place,
chunks.st: and his body was found in a different place,

chunks.en: they bring the head to the body,
chunks.st: they bring the head next to the body;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Eliezer.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says: They bring

chunks.en: they bring the body to the head.
chunks.st: the body next to the head.

summary: The judges measure from the person to the closest city. The Tanna'im argue from which part of him they measure.

chunks.en: From where did they measure?
chunks.st: From where on the body would they measure the distance?

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: From his belly button. Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: From his navel. Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.he: מֵחָטְמוֹ. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: From his nose. Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: From his nose. Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.en: From the place where he was killed: from his neck.
chunks.st: From the place where he became a slain person, which is from the neck.

summary: The elders of the closest city bring a young calf that never worked, take it down to a strong stream, and do the eglah arufah there. That ground may never be planted.
stIntro: The mishna continues to describe the ritual. After they would take the measurement,

chunks.en: The elders of Yerushalayim left and went away.
chunks.st: the Elders of Jerusalem took their leave and went away.

chunks.en: The elders of that city
chunks.st: The Elders of the city that is closest to the corpse

chunks.he: מְבִיאִין עֶגְלַת בָּקָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא עֻבַּד בָּהּ
chunks.en: bring a calf that was never made to work,
chunks.st: bring a heifer from cattle,

chunks.en: that never pulled a yoke.
chunks.st: which has not pulled a yoke.

chunks.en: A mum does not make it unfit,
chunks.st: But a blemish does not disqualify it,
chunks.stMore: because, unlike the description of the red heifer, the Torah does not state that it must be without blemish.

chunks.en: and they bring it down to a stream that is "eitan."
chunks.st: And they bring it down to a stream that is eitan.

chunks.en: "Eitan" means what it sounds like: strong.
chunks.st: Eitan in this context means as the word generally indicates, powerful. The stream must have a forceful flow.

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֵיתָן, כָּשֵׁר.
chunks.en: Even if it is not strong, it is kosher.
chunks.st: The mishna comments: Even if it is not forceful, it is a valid site for the ritual.

chunks.en: And they break its neck from behind with a big knife.
chunks.st: And they break the neck of the heifer from behind with a cleaver.

words.en: and they break the neck of

chunks.en: Its place may not be planted or worked,
chunks.st: And with regard to its place, where the heifer was standing when its neck was broken, it is prohibited for that ground to be sown or to be worked,

chunks.en: but you may comb flax there
chunks.st: but it is permitted to comb flax there

chunks.en: and cut stones there.
chunks.st: or to cut stones there.

summary: The elders wash their hands and say that they did not cause this death, and the Kohanim ask Hashem to forgive the Jewish people.

chunks.he: זִקְנֵי אוֹתָהּ הָעִיר רוֹחֲצִין אֶת יְדֵיהֶן
chunks.en: The elders of that city wash their hands
chunks.st: The Elders of that city would then wash their hands

chunks.en: in the water at the place of the eglah arufah,
chunks.st: in water in the place of the breaking of the neck of the heifer,

chunks.en: and they say (Devarim 21):
chunks.st: and they would recite:

chunks.he: יָדֵינוּ לֹא שָׁפְכֻה אֶת הַדָּם הַזֶּה
chunks.en: "Our hands did not spill this blood,
chunks.st: “Our hands did not spill this blood,

chunks.en: and our eyes did not see."
chunks.st: nor did our eyes see” (Deuteronomy 21:7).

chunks.en: Would anyone think
chunks.st: The mishna explains: But did it enter our minds

chunks.he: שֶׁזִּקְנֵי בֵית דִּין שׁוֹפְכֵי דָמִים הֵן,
chunks.en: that the elders of the Beis Din are killers?
chunks.st: that the Elders of the court are spillers of blood, that they must make such a declaration?

chunks.en: Rather, they mean: he did not come to us
chunks.st: Rather, they mean to declare that the victim did not come to us

chunks.en: and we sent him away without food,
chunks.st: and then we let him take his leave without food,

chunks.en: and we did not see him and leave him without walking with him.
chunks.st: and we did not see him and then leave him alone to depart without accompaniment.
chunks.stMore: They therefore attest that they took care of all his needs and are not responsible for his death even indirectly.

chunks.en: And the Kohanim say:
chunks.st: And the priests recite:

chunks.en: (Devarim 21) "Forgive Your people Yisrael,
chunks.st: “Forgive, Lord, Your people Israel,

chunks.en: whom You saved, Hashem,
chunks.st: whom You have redeemed,

chunks.en: and do not leave innocent blood
chunks.st: and suffer not innocent blood to remain

chunks.en: among Your people Yisrael."
chunks.st: in the midst of Your people Israel” (Deuteronomy 21:8).

chunks.en: They did not need to say
chunks.st: They did not have to recite

chunks.en: "And the blood will be forgiven for them,"
chunks.st: the conclusion of the verse: “And the blood shall be forgiven for them,”
chunks.stMore: as this is not part of the priests’ statement,

chunks.en: rather Ruach Hakodesh tells them:
chunks.st: but rather the Divine Spirit informs them:

chunks.en: "When you do this,
chunks.st: When you shall do so,

chunks.en: the blood is forgiven for you."
chunks.st: the blood is forgiven for you.

summary: If the killer is found before the eglah arufah, the calf goes back to the herd. If he is found after it, the calf is buried, and the killer is still punished.

chunks.he: נִמְצָא הַהוֹרֵג עַד שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֶרְפָה הָעֶגְלָה,
chunks.en: If the killer is found before the calf's neck is broken,
chunks.st: If the killer is found before the heifer’s neck was broken,

chunks.en: it goes out and grazes with the herd.
chunks.st: the heifer shall go out and graze among the herd.
chunks.stMore: It is not considered sacred at all, and it may rejoin the other animals.

chunks.en: Once the calf's neck was broken,
chunks.st: If the killer is found from the time when the heifer’s neck was broken,
chunks.stMore: even if the rest of the ritual has not yet been performed, it is prohibited to benefit from the animal, despite the killer having been found;

words.en: from when its neck was broken

chunks.en: it must be buried in its place,
chunks.st: it should be buried in its place.

chunks.en: because it came for a doubt from the start,
chunks.st: This is because the heifer initially came for uncertainty, as the killer was unknown,

chunks.en: and it atoned for its doubt and finished its job.
chunks.st: and it atoned for its uncertainty and left,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it fulfilled its purpose of bringing atonement and is considered a heifer whose neck is broken in all regards.

chunks.he: נֶעֶרְפָה הָעֶגְלָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִמְצָא הַהוֹרֵג,
chunks.en: If the calf's neck was broken and after that the killer was found,
chunks.st: If the heifer’s neck was broken and afterward the killer was found,

chunks.en: he still gets the death punishment.
chunks.st: he is killed. The ritual does not atone for him.

summary: If witnesses argue about whether someone saw the killer, they still do the eglah arufah, unless two witnesses say they saw him.

chunks.he: עֵד אֶחָד אוֹמֵר רָאִיתִי אֶת הַהוֹרֵג,
chunks.en: If one witness says, "I saw the killer,"
chunks.st: one witness says: I saw the killer,

chunks.en: and one witness says, "You did not see,"
chunks.st: and one other witness says: You did not see him; or if

chunks.en: or a woman says, "I saw,"
chunks.st: a woman says: I saw,

chunks.en: and a woman says, "You did not see,"
chunks.st: and another woman says: You did not see,

chunks.en: they do the eglah arufah.
chunks.st: they would break the neck
chunks.stMore: of the heifer, as without clear testimony about the identity of the killer the ritual is performed.

chunks.en: If one witness says, "I saw,"
chunks.st: Similarly, if one witness says: I saw the killer,

chunks.en: and two say, "You did not see,"
chunks.st: and two witnesses say: You did not see,

chunks.en: they do the eglah arufah.
chunks.st: they would break the neck of the heifer, as the pair is relied upon.

chunks.en: If two say, "We saw,"
chunks.st: If two witnesses say: We saw the killer,

chunks.en: and one says to them, "You did not see,"
chunks.st: and one witness says to them: You did not see,

chunks.en: they do not do the eglah arufah.
chunks.st: they would not break the neck
chunks.stMore: of the heifer, as there are two witnesses to the identity of the killer.

summary: When there were many killers, the eglah arufah stopped, and when there were many sinners, the bitter water stopped. When two great Sages died, the "eshkolos" came to an end.

chunks.en: When the killers became many,
chunks.st: From the time when murderers proliferated,

chunks.en: the eglah arufah stopped.
chunks.st: the ritual of the heifer whose neck is broken was nullified.
chunks.stMore: The ritual was performed only when the identity of the murderer was completely unknown. Once there were many known murderers, the conditions for the performance of the ritual were no longer present, as the probable identity of the murderer was known.

chunks.en: When Eliezer ben Dinai came,
chunks.st: From the time when Eliezer ben Dinai,

chunks.en: who was also called Techinah ben Perishah,
chunks.st: who was also called Teḥina ben Perisha, came,

chunks.en: they started calling him "son of the killer."
chunks.st: they renamed him: Son of a murderer.
chunks.stMore: This is an example of a publicly known murderer. The mishna teaches a similar occurrence:

chunks.en: When the sinners became many,
chunks.st: From the time when adulterers proliferated,

words.note: People who did the sin of a forbidden relationship.

chunks.en: the bitter water stopped.
chunks.st: the performance of the ritual of the bitter waters was nullified;
chunks.stMore: they would not administer the bitter waters to the sota.

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai stopped it,
chunks.st: And it was Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Zakkai who nullified it,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Hoshea 4):
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.he: לֹא אֶפְקוֹד עַל בְּנוֹתֵיכֶם כִּי תִזְנֶינָה
chunks.en: "I will not punish your daughters when they sin,
chunks.st: “I will not punish your daughters when they commit harlotry,

chunks.en: nor your daughters-in-law when they sin,
chunks.st: nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery;

chunks.en: because they (the men) also..."
chunks.explain: When the husbands sin too, the wives are not tested.
chunks.st: for they
chunks.stMore: consort with lewd women” (Hosea 4:14), meaning that when the husbands are adulterers, the wives are not punished for their own adultery.

chunks.he: מִשֶּׁמֵּת יוֹסֵי בֶן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵדָה
chunks.en: When Yosei ben Yoezer of Tzeredah
chunks.st: From the time when Yosei ben Yo’ezer of Tzereida

chunks.en: and Yosei ben Yochanan of Yerushalayim died,
chunks.st: and Yosei ben Yehuda of Jerusalem died,

chunks.en: the "eshkolos" (clusters) came to an end,
chunks.explain: A name for the greatest Sages of those times.
chunks.st: the clusters ceased,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they were the last of the clusters, as explained in the Gemara,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Michah 7):
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "There is no cluster to eat,
chunks.st: “There is no cluster to eat;

chunks.en: no first fig that my soul wants."
chunks.st: nor first-ripe fig that my soul desires” (Micah 7:1).

summary: Yochanan the Kohen Gadol stopped some things that were done before him, and in his days everyone was careful to take maaser.
stIntro: The mishna continues in the same vein:

chunks.he: יוֹחָנָן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הֶעֱבִיר הוֹדָיַת הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
chunks.en: Yochanan the Kohen Gadol stopped the declaration about maaser.
chunks.st: Yoḥanan the High Priest took away the declaration of the tithe.
chunks.stMore: After his time, no one recited the passage about the elimination of tithes that had previously been said at the end of a three-year tithing cycle.

chunks.en: He also stopped
chunks.st: He also nullified the actions of

chunks.en: the "wakers" and the "knockers."
chunks.explain: Things that were done in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: the awakeners and the strikers at the Temple.

chunks.he: עַד יָמָיו הָיָה פַטִּישׁ מַכֶּה בִירוּשָׁלַיִם.
chunks.en: Until his days, a hammer would bang in Yerushalayim (on Chol Hamoed).
chunks.st: Until his days the hammer of smiths would strike in Jerusalem
chunks.stMore: on the intermediate days of a Festival, but he banned the practice.

chunks.en: And in his days, no one needed
chunks.st: And furthermore, in his days there was no need

chunks.en: to ask about demai.
chunks.st: to inquire about doubtfully tithed produce [demai],
chunks.stMore: as everyone was careful to tithe. This mishna continues with the list of items that were nullified.

words.note: Food that may not have had maaser taken from it.

summary: When the Sanhedrin stopped, singing at parties with wine was stopped too.

chunks.en: When the Sanhedrin stopped,
chunks.st: From the time when the Sanhedrin ceased

chunks.en: singing stopped at parties,
chunks.st: song was also nullified from the places of feasts,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it was no longer permitted to sing at a feast where wine was served,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Yeshayahu 24):
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "They shall not drink wine with song..."
chunks.st: “With song they shall not drink wine” (Isaiah 24:9).

summary: After the first Nevi'im died and the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed, many good things stopped, and the world lost some of its bracha.

chunks.en: When the first Nevi'im died,
chunks.st: From the time when the early prophets died

chunks.en: the Urim VeTumim stopped.
chunks.st: the Urim VeTummim was nullified.

chunks.en: When the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: From the time when the Second Temple was destroyed

chunks.en: the shamir and the sweet honeycomb stopped,
chunks.st: the shamir worm ceased to exist and also the sweetness of the honeycomb,
chunks.stMore: as the verse says with regard to the laws of the Torah: “More to be desired are they than gold, indeed, than much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb” (Psalms 19:11).

chunks.en: and faithful people came to an end,
chunks.st: And men of faith ceased from being among the Jewish people,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Tehillim 12):
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.he: הוֹשִׁיעָה ה' כִּי גָמַר חָסִיד וְגוֹ'.
chunks.en: "Help, Hashem, for the pious man is gone..."
chunks.st: “Help, Lord, for the pious man is finished;
chunks.stMore: for the faithful fail from among the children of men” (Psalms 12:2).

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

chunks.en: says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua,
chunks.st: says that Rabbi Yehoshua testified:

chunks.en: From the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: From the day the Temple was destroyed

chunks.en: there is no day without a curse,
chunks.st: there is no day that does not include some form of curse.

chunks.en: and the dew does not come down for bracha,
chunks.st: And since then the dew has not descended for blessing,

chunks.en: and the taste was taken from fruit.
chunks.st: and the taste has been removed from fruit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: Also the richness was taken from fruit.
chunks.st: Since then, the fat of fruit has also been removed.

summary: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar and the Sages say which sins took away the good taste of fruit and grain.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Since then,

chunks.he: הַטָּהֳרָה נָטְלָה אֶת הַטַּעַם וְאֶת הָרֵיחַ.
chunks.en: Losing taharah took away the taste and the smell.
chunks.st: the lost purity has removed the taste and the aroma from fruit;

chunks.en: Not taking maaser took away the richness of the grain.
chunks.st: the tithes that were not separated have removed the fat of the grain.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Sages say:

chunks.en: Forbidden relationships and witchcraft finished everything.
chunks.st: Promiscuity and witchcraft have consumed it all.

summary: During three wars, the Sages made sad rules: no crowns for a chassan or a kallah, no drums, and no teaching children Greek.

chunks.en: In the war of Aspasyanus, they made a rule
chunks.st: In the war [pulemus] of Vespasian the Sages decreed

chunks.en: against crowns for chassanim,
chunks.st: upon the crowns of bridegrooms,
chunks.stMore: i.e., that bridegrooms may no longer wear crowns,

chunks.en: and against the drum.
chunks.st: and upon the drums,
chunks.stMore: meaning they also banned the playing of drums.

chunks.en: In the war of Titus, they made a rule
chunks.st: In the war of Titus they also decreed

chunks.en: against crowns for kallos,
chunks.st: upon the crowns of brides,

chunks.he: וְשֶׁלֹא יְלַמֵּד אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ יְוָנִית.
chunks.en: and that a person should not teach his son Greek.
chunks.st: and they decreed that a person should not teach his son Greek.

chunks.en: In the last war,
chunks.st: In the last war, meaning the bar Kokheva revolt,

chunks.en: they made a rule that a kallah may not go out
chunks.st: they decreed that a bride may not go out

chunks.en: in a covered chair inside the city.
chunks.st: in a palanquin inside the city,

chunks.en: But our Rabbis allowed a kallah to go out
chunks.st: but our Sages permitted a bride to go out

chunks.en: in a covered chair inside the city.
chunks.st: in a palanquin inside the city, as this helps the bride maintain her modesty.

summary: The mishnah tells what was lost when each great Sage died, describes the hard times before Mashiach, and ends with Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair's ladder of good traits that leads all the way to techiyas hameisim.
stIntro: The mishna lists more things that ceased:

chunks.en: When Rabbi Meir died,
chunks.st: From the time when Rabbi Meir died,

chunks.en: the people who told meshalim stopped.
chunks.st: those who relate parables ceased;

words.note: Parables: stories that teach a lesson.

chunks.en: When Ben Azzai died,
chunks.st: from the time when ben Azzai died,

chunks.en: the hard-working learners stopped.
chunks.st: the diligent ceased;

chunks.en: When Ben Zoma died,
chunks.st: from the time when ben Zoma died,

chunks.en: the darshanim stopped.
chunks.st: the exegetists ceased;

chunks.en: When Rabbi Yehoshua died,
chunks.st: from the time when Rabbi Yehoshua died,

chunks.en: goodness stopped from the world.
chunks.st: goodness ceased from the world;

chunks.en: When Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel died,
chunks.st: from the time when Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel died,

chunks.en: locusts came and troubles grew.
chunks.st: locusts come and troubles multiplied;

chunks.en: When Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah died,
chunks.st: from the time when Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya died,

chunks.en: the Sages stopped being rich.
chunks.st: the sages ceased to be wealthy;

chunks.en: When Rabbi Akiva died,
chunks.st: from the time when Rabbi Akiva died,

chunks.en: the honor of the Torah stopped.
chunks.st: the honor of the Torah ceased;

chunks.en: When Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa died,
chunks.st: from the time when Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa died,

chunks.en: the men of wonderful deeds stopped.
chunks.st: the men of wondrous action ceased;

chunks.en: When Rabbi Yosei Ketanusa died,
chunks.st: from the time when Rabbi Yosei the Small died,

chunks.en: the chassidim stopped.
chunks.st: the pious were no more.

chunks.en: And why was he called Ketanusa ("the small")?
chunks.st: And why was he called the Small?

chunks.en: Because he was the smallest of the chassidim.
chunks.st: Because he was the smallest of the pious,
chunks.stMore: meaning he was one of the least important of the pious men.

chunks.en: When Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai died,
chunks.st: From the time when Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai died,

chunks.en: the shine of wisdom stopped.
chunks.st: the glory of wisdom ceased;

chunks.en: When Rabban Gamliel the Elder died,
chunks.st: from the time when Rabban Gamliel the Elder died,

chunks.he: בָּטַל כְּבוֹד הַתּוֹרָה וּמֵתָה טָהֳרָה וּפְרִישׁוּת.
chunks.en: the honor of the Torah stopped, and purity and perishus died.
chunks.st: the honor of the Torah ceased, and purity and asceticism died.

chunks.en: When Rabbi Yishmael ben Pavi died,
chunks.st: From the time when Rabbi Yishmael ben Pavi died,

chunks.en: the shine of the Kehunah stopped.
chunks.st: the glory of the priesthood ceased;

chunks.en: When Rebbi died,
chunks.st: from the time when Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi died,

chunks.en: humility and fear of sin stopped.
chunks.st: humility and fear of sin ceased.

chunks.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir says:

chunks.en: When the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: From the time when the Second Temple was destroyed,

chunks.en: the chaverim and noble people were ashamed,
chunks.st: the ḥaverim and free men of noble lineage were ashamed,

chunks.en: and covered their heads,
chunks.st: and their heads were covered in shame,

chunks.en: and men of good deeds became fewer,
chunks.st: and men of action dwindled,

chunks.en: and strong-armed people and smooth talkers grew stronger,
chunks.st: and violent and smooth-talking men gained the upper hand,

chunks.en: and no one explains and no one seeks,
chunks.st: and none seek, and none ask,

chunks.en: and no one asks.
chunks.st: and none inquire of the fear of Heaven.

chunks.en: On whom can we lean?
chunks.st: Upon whom is there for us to rely?

chunks.en: On our Father in Heaven.
chunks.st: Only upon our Father in Heaven.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer HaGadol says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:

chunks.en: From the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: From the day the Second Temple was destroyed, the generations have deteriorated:

chunks.en: the Sages began to be like teachers of children,
chunks.st: Scholars have begun to become like scribes that teach children,

chunks.en: and the teachers like shamashim,
chunks.st: and scribes have become like beadles,

chunks.en: and shamashim like simple people,
chunks.st: and beadles have become like ignoramuses,

chunks.en: and simple people are getting weaker and weaker,
chunks.st: and ignoramuses are increasingly diminished,

chunks.en: and no one seeks.
chunks.st: and none ask and none seek.

chunks.en: On whom can we lean?
chunks.st: Upon whom is there to rely?

chunks.en: On our Father in Heaven.
chunks.st: Only upon our Father in Heaven.

chunks.en: Before Mashiach comes, chutzpah will grow,
chunks.st: He also said: In the times of the approach of the Messiah, impudence will increase

chunks.en: and prices will go way up.
chunks.st: and high costs will pile up.

chunks.en: The vine will give its fruit, but wine will be expensive,
chunks.st: Although the vine shall bring forth its fruit, wine will nevertheless be expensive.

chunks.en: and the kingdom will turn away from emunah,
chunks.st: And the monarchy shall turn to heresy,

chunks.en: and no one will rebuke.
chunks.st: and there will be no one to give reproof about this.

chunks.en: The Sages' meeting place will become a place of sin,
chunks.st: The meeting place of the Sages will become a place of promiscuity,

chunks.en: and the Galil will be destroyed,
chunks.st: and the Galilee shall be destroyed,

chunks.en: and the Gavlan will be empty,
chunks.st: and the Gavlan will be desolate,

chunks.en: and the people of the border will go around from city to city,
chunks.st: and the men of the border shall go round from city to city to seek charity,

chunks.en: and no one will be kind to them.
chunks.st: but they will find no mercy.

chunks.en: The wisdom of the Sages will go bad,
chunks.st: And the wisdom of scribes will putrefy,

chunks.en: people who fear sin will be hated,
chunks.st: and people who fear sin will be held in disgust,

chunks.en: and truth will be missing.
chunks.st: and the truth will be absent.

chunks.en: Young people will embarrass old people,
chunks.st: The youth will shame the face of elders,

chunks.en: old people will stand up for children.
chunks.st: elders will stand before minors.

chunks.en: (Michah 7) A son will shame his father,
chunks.st: Normal family relations will be ruined: A son will disgrace a father;

chunks.en: a daughter will rise up against her mother,
chunks.st: a daughter will rise up against her mother,

chunks.en: a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law,
chunks.st: a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

chunks.en: a man's enemies will be the people of his own house.
chunks.st: A man’s enemies will be the members of his household.

chunks.en: The face of the generation will be like the face of a dog,
chunks.st: The face of the generation will be like the face of a dog;

chunks.en: a son will not be ashamed before his father.
chunks.st: a son will no longer be ashamed before his father.

chunks.en: And on whom can we lean?
chunks.st: And upon what is there for us to rely?

chunks.en: On our Father in Heaven.
chunks.st: Only upon our Father in heaven.

chunks.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir says: Torah study leads to care in the performance of mitzvot.

chunks.en: Being quick (to do mitzvos) leads to being clean (from sin),
chunks.st: Care in the performance of mitzvot leads to diligence in their observance.

chunks.en: being clean leads to purity,
chunks.st: Diligence leads to cleanliness of the soul.

chunks.en: purity leads to perishus,
chunks.st: Cleanliness of the soul leads to abstention from all evil.

chunks.en: perishus leads to holiness,
chunks.st: Abstention from evil leads to purity and the elimination of all base desires.

chunks.en: holiness leads to humility,
chunks.st: Purity leads to piety.

chunks.en: humility leads to fear of sin,
chunks.st: Piety leads to humility.

chunks.en: fear of sin leads to chassidus,
chunks.st: Humility leads to fear of sin.

chunks.en: chassidus leads to Ruach Hakodesh,
chunks.st: Fear of sin leads to holiness.

chunks.he: וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מְבִיאָה לִידֵי תְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים,
chunks.en: Ruach Hakodesh leads to techiyas hameisim,
chunks.explain: Techiyas hameisim: when the dead will come back to life.
chunks.st: Holiness leads to the Divine Spirit.

chunks.en: through Eliyahu, may he be remembered for good. Amen!
